smell_validity.evidence: Inlining genuinely scatters one responsibility — client-flavor detection plus sharded subscribe/unsubscribe/publish dispatch and legacy registry bookkeeping — across nine sites in three files, and the copies diverge materially (registry setup vs cleanup, promise shapes), so a conceptual compat change needs coordinated edits. Weaker edge: the classic-adapter gates were already inline pre-injection; the capability swap adds drift, not new scattering.

maintenance_impact.evidence: Client-flavor compatibility is recurring work (five supported client families, new node-redis majors rename methods), so nine drifted copies plus directly manipulating the exported registry symbol turn every compat change into a coordinated hunt where missed copies cause inconsistent behavior. Consolidation restores the shared module's ownership boundary, making future cross-flavor work single-point and safer, well beyond tidying.

development_plausibility.evidence: The fragments are verbatim bodies of the real helpers, matching file conventions (private handler methods, compat comment, TypeScript style); deleting the now-callless helpers and exporting kHandlers mirror believable cleanup drift. Slight scaffolding remains: five near-identical ten-line registry blocks within one file and the same probe repeated at every site read more assembled than evolved.

prompt_accuracy.evidence: Scope, finished state and exclusions agree: one detection owner, one helper per sharded command, classic gates through shared detection, remove direct kHandlers manipulation, keep the server-count path untouched; the acceptance boundary names every client/mode combination and the at-most-once listener rule, ruling out partial cleanups and redesign. One slip: it claims the classic gates probe a different capability than the shared helper, but both probe sSubscribe.

semantic_diversity.evidence: Three purposes require genuinely different decisions: subscribe (idempotent registry creation, buffer flag, handler argument), unsubscribe (registry deletion over string versus array inputs in close), publish (registry-independent, site-specific resolved values '' versus raw), plus detection gating. Each purpose needs its own code-supported decision such as object reuse, cleanup or return contracts, not one repeated edit.

localization_burden.evidence: Repair decisions combine util and two adapters: PUBSUB's helper use must be classified as already-correct, kHandlers/smessageBuffer callback registration and subscriptionMode-driven room-channel registration must be understood, and the classic adapter's own redisListeners map is a plausible-looking demux that must stay excluded. However, a single capability grep (sSubscribe/ssubscribe/kHandlers) surfaces nearly all sites, capping the burden.

repair_coordination.evidence: Centralized registry creation interlocks with cleanup obligations in onRoomDeleted, close()'s array path and message dispatch, and the probe outcome governs buffer flag, handler argument and cleanup equally across sites. Concrete partial repair: centralize subscribe without the idempotent guard — the first subscription works, the constructor's second call attaches a second smessageBuffer listener and duplicates delivery; each stage alone succeeds.

mechanical_resistance.evidence: Nine problem locations. The best single uniform rule — recreate a subscribe helper and replace the three identical fragments (both constructor sites and onRoomCreated) — covers about 33%; unsubscribe, publish and gate sites need different code (registry handling, promise shapes, probe call), and reconnecting the surviving isRedisV4Client covers only the two classic gates.

behavioral_risk.evidence: Wrong edits dropping the buffer flag, duplicating listener attaches, or selecting the wrong flavor branch break binary broadcasts or delivery counts and are caught by the existing 11-variant suite, which explicitly asserts Buffer payloads. But dropping unsubscribe-side registry cleanup compiles, passes ordinary calls, and silently leaves stale legacy handler entries after dynamic room deletion — a special-state failure no assertion checks.

recommendation_reason: Deterministic validation passed and every Quality dimension meets the retention threshold.
